newsitem.title: JAPAN: Greenspan, Mitsuzuka reaffirm stance on forex -- MOF.
newsitem.headline: Greenspan, Mitsuzuka reaffirm stance on forex -- MOF.

text.p: Japan's Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka and U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan reaffirmed the basic stance of their two countries toward the foreign exchange market during a meeting on Monday morning, senior officials of Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) said.
The officials, however, declined to elaborate.

Last Thursday, Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the Finance Ministry's International Finance Bureau, told reporters that Japan's policy on foreign exchange had not changed and added that Tokyo welcomed developments in the currency markets since April 1995.
Sakakibara also said that cooperation among the Group of Seven industrialised nations on currencies remained unchanged.
Also on Thursday, U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin reiterated his support for a strong dollar, saying it was in U.S. interests.
